title: The Ito Integral with Respect to Brownian Motion

items.title: Continuous-time adapted processes and martingales
items.statement: Assume AC. On a filtered probability space, X is adapted when X_t is F_t-measurable; it is a martingale when integrable and E[X_t|F_s]=X_s for s<=t, and a local martingale when stopping times tau_n increase to infinity almost surely and each X^{tau_n}-X_0 is a martingale. Continuous, square-integrable and L2-bounded have their usual path and integrability meanings.
items.strategy: Reconcile the all-pairs supplier with process notation, verify deterministic times are stopping times, and record localization of X-X_0 explicitly.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Sections 4.1 and 5.4

items.title: Progressively measurable and predictable processes
items.statement: H is progressively measurable if its restriction to [0,t] times Omega is B([0,t]) tensor F_t measurable for every t. The predictable sigma-algebra is generated by (s,t] times A, A in F_s, and {0} times A, A in F_0; H is predictable when measurable for it.
items.strategy: Check the generator and time-zero convention; derive deterministic-time adaptedness and finite-horizon product measurability.
items.axiom_base: ZF

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Section 5.1

items.title: Adapted continuous processes are progressively measurable
items.statement: Every real adapted process with continuous sample paths is progressively measurable and predictable, including at time zero under the generator convention {0} times F_0.
items.strategy: On each [0,T], approximate at positive time by left-endpoint dyadic steps. These are predictable and product measurable; path continuity gives pointwise convergence on (0,T]. At time zero use the F_0-measurable section on the generator {0} times F_0. Pointwise-limit measurability closes both claims.
items.axiom_base: ZF

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Section 5.1

items.title: Elementary predictable Brownian integrands
items.statement: Assume AC. Fix Brownian motion B on a filtered probability space with respect to which B is Brownian, in particular the usual augmented natural Brownian filtration used below. On [0,T], an elementary predictable integrand is H_s=sum xi_k 1_(t_k,t_{k+1}](s), where 0=t_0<...<t_m=T and bounded xi_k is F_{t_k}-measurable; endpoint values are immaterial modulo dt tensor P.
items.strategy: Verify predictability from the generating rectangles, square integrability from boundedness, and endpoint irrelevance from Lebesgue-null finite sets.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2.2

items.title: Ito integral of an elementary predictable process
items.statement: Assume AC. For elementary H define I_t(H)=sum xi_k(B_{t wedge t_{k+1}}-B_{t wedge t_k}) and write it as integral_0^t H_s dB_s.
items.strategy: Define the finite sum on the common Brownian continuity event and check adaptedness and continuity termwise.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2.2

items.title: Elementary Ito integrals do not depend on step representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Two elementary representations equal dt tensor P almost everywhere have almost surely equal terminal Ito sums; deterministic partition refinement changes nothing.
items.strategy: Use a common refinement. For their difference expand the expected squared sum; conditional centering kills cross terms and Brownian variance turns diagonal terms into its product-L2 energy, which is zero by Tonelli.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Definition 5.20 and Lemma 5.22

items.title: Ito isometry for elementary integrands
items.statement: Assume AC. For elementary predictable H, I_t(H) is a continuous square-integrable martingale and E[I_t(H)^2]=E integral_0^t H_s^2 ds.
items.strategy: Refine to include s,t. Conditional centering proves the martingale identity. Expanding the square kills cross terms and evaluates each diagonal term as E[xi_k^2]Delta t_k; continuity is pathwise.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Proposition 3.2.1

items.title: Cross Ito isometry
items.statement: Assume AC. For elementary predictable H,K, E[I_t(H)I_t(K)]=E integral_0^t H_sK_s ds.
items.strategy: Apply the isometry to H+K, subtract the identities for H and K, and expand both squares.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Lemma 5.22

items.title: Density of elementary predictable processes in predictable L2
items.statement: Assume AC. On every finite horizon, bounded elementary predictable processes are dense in predictable L2(dt tensor P), modulo product-almost-everywhere equality.
items.strategy: Predictable generating rectangles have elementary indicators and form a pi-system containing the whole finite product (with the time-zero generator harmless modulo dt tensor P). Let D be the predictable sets whose indicators are L2-limits of bounded elementary processes. D contains that pi-system, is closed under complements, and is closed under countable disjoint unions: finite partial unions remain elementary-approximable, and dominated convergence sends their indicators to the union in L2. Thus D is a lambda-system; Dynkin pi-lambda gives every predictable set. Finite simple approximation, truncation, and Riesz-Fischer then give density for arbitrary predictable L2 classes.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Lemmas 5.21-5.23

items.title: Ito integral for square-integrable predictable processes
items.statement: Assume AC. For predictable H in L2([0,T] times Omega), choose elementary H^n converging in predictable L2 and define integral_0^T H_s dB_s as the L2(Omega) limit of I_T(H^n); at t use 1_[0,t]H.
items.strategy: Density supplies an approximation, the isometry makes its images Cauchy, and Riesz-Fischer supplies their L2 limit. Keep domain and range as a.e. quotient classes.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Definition 5.25

items.title: The general Ito integral is well defined
items.statement: Assume AC. The L2 Ito integral is independent of elementary approximation and of the predictable dt tensor P representative.
items.strategy: Interlace two approximations; isometry makes the distance of image limits equal the vanishing domain distance. Product-a.e.-equal representatives have distance zero.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Definition 5.25 and Theorem 5.26

items.title: Ito isometry and linearity in predictable L2
items.statement: Assume AC. H maps linearly and isometrically to integral_0^t H dB in mean-zero L2(Omega), and E[(integral H dB)(integral K dB)]=E integral HK ds.
items.strategy: Approximate H,K simultaneously; pass elementary linearity and the cross identity through L2 limits, using Cauchy-Schwarz for products. L2 limits preserve zero expectation.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Sections 3.2.2-3.2.3

items.title: The Ito integral process has a continuous martingale version
items.statement: Assume AC. If H is predictable and square-integrable on finite horizons, M_t=integral_0^t H_s dB_s has an adapted continuous square-integrable-martingale version, unique up to indistinguishability.
items.strategy: Choose elementary approximants with summable L2 errors. Discrete Doob on increasing rational grids yields the supremum bound; a subsequence converges uniformly almost surely to a continuous adapted process. Fixed-time L2 limits identify it and pass conditional expectations. Diagonalize over integer horizons; rational equality plus continuity proves uniqueness.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Theorem 5.26
Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Proposition 3.2.4

items.title: Doob maximal bound for the Ito integral
items.statement: Assume AC. E sup_{t<=T}|integral_0^t H_s dB_s|^2 <=4 E integral_0^T H_s^2 ds for predictable square-integrable H.
items.strategy: Apply discrete Doob L2 on increasing rational grids. Continuity and monotone convergence pass grid maxima to the path supremum, then terminal isometry gives the bound.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Proposition 3.2.4

items.title: Locally square-integrable predictable Brownian integrands
items.statement: Assume AC. Predictable H is locally square-integrable when integral_0^t H_s^2ds is finite almost surely for every finite t. Set tau_n=inf{t:integral_0^t H_s^2ds>=n} wedge n.
items.strategy: Tonelli gives measurable accumulated energy; its continuous adapted paths show tau_n is a stopping time. Local finiteness makes tau_n increase to infinity almost surely.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Sections 5.4-5.5

items.title: Localized Ito integral
items.statement: Assume AC. Every locally square-integrable predictable H has a continuous local-martingale integral H dot B, characterized by its stopped square-integrable integrals and independent of the localizing sequence up to indistinguishability.
items.strategy: Construct finite-energy stopped integrals. Isometry proves agreement on overlaps; continuity upgrades rational-time equality to indistinguishability. Patch them, then compare pairwise minima for any second localization. The stopped pieces prove the local-martingale property.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Lemma 5.33 and Theorem 5.36

items.title: Stopping an Ito integral
items.statement: Assume AC. For a stopping time tau and locally square-integrable predictable H, (H dot B)_{t wedge tau}=integral_0^t 1_{s<=tau}H_s dB_s up to indistinguishability.
items.strategy: Prove it for elementary H and finite-valued tau by refinement. Approximate tau from above dyadically and H in L2; isometry and the maximal bound give uniform convergence in probability. Localize and use continuity.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Lemma 5.28 and Theorem 5.36

items.title: Quadratic variation of an Ito integral
items.statement: Assume AC. If M=H dot B, then along every deterministic partition sequence with mesh tending to zero, squared-increment partial sums converge uniformly in probability on [0,T] to [M]_t=integral_0^t H_s^2ds.
items.strategy: For arbitrary deterministic Brownian partitions, centered squared increments form a discrete martingale with variance at most 2T times mesh; Doob and continuity give uniform convergence. Prove the claim blockwise for elementary H. For L2 limits, Cauchy-Schwarz bounds differences of square sums by the product of sum-squares for M-M^n and M+M^n; isometry controls them. Finish by energy localization.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Section 5.8 and Lemma 5.77
Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Theorem 3.2.6

items.title: Deterministic Ito integrals are Gaussian
items.statement: Assume AC. For deterministic h in L2[0,T], integral h dB is centered normal with variance integral h^2. Finite families are jointly Gaussian with covariance integral hk.
items.strategy: Step functions give linear combinations of independent Gaussian increments. Approximate h in deterministic L2; isometry gives convergence in probability and the variances converge. The Gaussian-parameter weak-convergence example identifies the limit law, including zero variance. Apply the same argument to every scalar linear combination of a finite family and use the stated Cramer-Wold definition; cross isometry yields the covariance integral.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2 and Exercise 3.8

title: The Ito Integral with Respect to Brownian Motion — Examples

items.title: A deterministic step integrand
items.statement: Assume AC. For h=sum a_k 1_(t_k,t_{k+1}], its Ito integral is sum a_k(B_{t wedge t_{k+1}}-B_{t wedge t_k}) and at T is N(0,sum a_k^2 Delta t_k).
items.strategy: Substitute into the elementary definition and evaluate the step function's L2 norm in the Gaussian corollary.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2.2

items.title: Indicator of a stopping interval
items.statement: Assume AC. For every stopping time tau, integral_0^t 1_{s<=tau}dB_s=B_{t wedge tau}-B_0 up to indistinguishability.
items.strategy: Apply stopping to H=1, whose elementary integral is B_t-B_0.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2.3

items.title: Covariance of deterministic Ito integrals
items.statement: Assume AC. For deterministic h,k in L2[0,T], Cov(integral h dB,integral k dB)=integral hk; disjoint supports therefore give independent integrals.
items.strategy: Use cross isometry; joint Gaussianity turns zero covariance into independence.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Lemma 5.22

items.title: Integral of Brownian motion against itself
items.statement: Assume AC. Up to indistinguishability, for every t>=0, integral_0^t B_s dB_s=(B_t^2-t)/2.
items.strategy: Left-dyadic steps converge to B in predictable L2. Use 2 sum B_left Delta B=B_t^2-sum(Delta B)^2 and uniform dyadic quadratic variation. Prove at rational times and extend by continuity, without the later Ito-formula result.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, equation (3.8)

items.title: A deterministic time-changed quadratic variation
items.statement: Assume AC. For M_t=integral_0^t s dB_s, [M]_t=t^3/3.
items.strategy: Apply the quadratic-variation theorem to H_s=s and integrate s squared.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Theorem 3.2.6

items.title: A nonadapted step integrand breaks the Ito isometry
items.statement: Assume AC. For T>0, naively taking H_s=1_{|B_T|>sqrt(T)} on (0,T] gives E[H^2B_T^2]>T E[H^2], contrary to Ito isometry; H is not F_0-measurable.
items.strategy: On A={|B_T|>sqrt(T)}, B_T^2>T and P(A)>0 from the normal density. The strict expectation inequality follows and the terminal coefficient violates predictability.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2.2

items.title: Bounded-variation Riemann-Stieltjes theory does not construct the Brownian Ito integral
items.statement: Assume AC. Almost surely Brownian paths have infinite total variation on every nondegenerate compact interval, so the classical bounded-variation construction of integral f dg for every continuous f cannot define Brownian Ito integration pathwise.
items.strategy: Apply the Brownian infinite-variation corollary. Claim only failure of the bounded-variation construction, not nonexistence of every special pathwise integral.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 2.8

items.title: Product-measure equality is not pointwise equality
items.statement: Assume AC. H(t,omega)=1_{t=1/2} and K=0 are deterministic predictable processes equal dt tensor P almost everywhere, but as raw processes they differ exactly on {1/2} times Omega (only their t=1/2 sections differ); their Ito integrals agree.
items.strategy: The singleton {1/2} is Lebesgue null and its deterministic indicator is predictable. General-integral well-definedness identifies the product-a.e. classes despite the explicitly isolated raw pointwise discrepancy.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Definition 5.25

items.title: Continuous Brownian Ito processes
items.statement: Assume AC. A real continuous Brownian Ito process is X_t=X_0+integral_0^t b_s ds+integral_0^t sigma_s dB_s, where X_0 is finite and F_0-measurable, b is real progressively measurable with integral_0^t |b_s|ds finite a.s., and sigma is real predictable with integral_0^t sigma_s^2ds finite a.s. for every finite t. In dimension d driven by m-dimensional Brownian motion, X_0 is finite F_0-measurable in R^d, b takes values in R^d, and sigma takes values in R^{d times m}, with the same componentwise local integrability conditions.
items.strategy: Use pathwise Lebesgue integration for b and the localized Ito integral for each row of sigma; finite componentwise sums give continuity and adaptedness. The displayed dimensions prevent an untyped matrix convention.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Section 5.9

items.title: Quadratic covariation of Brownian Ito processes
items.statement: For continuous X,Y, [X,Y] is a single continuous process such that, for every deterministic partition sequence whose mesh tends to zero, the paired-increment partial-sum processes converge to it uniformly in probability on every compact time interval; when such a common limit exists write [X]=[X,X].
items.strategy: Specify the stopped partial-sum convention and require the same UCP limit for every deterministic vanishing-mesh sequence, rather than a sequence-dependent value. Record polarization 4[X,Y]=[X+Y]-[X-Y] whenever these common quadratic variations exist.
items.axiom_base: ZF

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Definition 5.62 and Theorem 5.64

items.title: Quadratic covariation of Brownian Ito processes
items.statement: Assume AC. If dX^i=b^idt+sum_k sigma^{ik}dB^k, then [X^i,X^j]_t=sum_k integral_0^t sigma_s^{ik}sigma_s^{jk}ds; continuous finite-variation parts have zero covariation with continuous Ito martingale parts.
items.strategy: For terms driven by the same Brownian coordinate, polarize the scalar quadratic-variation theorem. For distinct coordinates, prove the elementary cross-increment sums converge to zero by conditional centering and an L2 mesh bound, then pass through predictable-L2 approximation and localization. Bound finite-variation cross sums by maximum martingale increment times total variation, which vanishes after localization by continuity.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Section 5.8

items.title: Integration by parts for Brownian Ito processes
items.statement: Assume AC. For continuous Brownian Ito processes X,Y, X_tY_t=X_0Y_0+integral X_sdY_s+integral Y_sdX_s+[X,Y]_t, with differential integrals expanded into Lebesgue and Ito parts.
items.strategy: Sum the exact partition identity Delta(XY)=X_left Delta Y+Y_left Delta X+Delta X Delta Y. Covariation handles the last sum; localized left-step convergence in time-L1 and predictable-L2 handles the first two.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, equation (5.63)

items.title: One-dimensional Ito formula
items.statement: Assume AC. Let X be a real continuous Brownian Ito process dX_t=b_tdt+sigma_tdB_t and let f belong to C^{1,2}([0,infinity) times R). Then, up to indistinguishability, for every t>=0, f(t,X_t)=f(0,X_0)+integral_0^t (f_t+b f_x+(sigma^2/2)f_xx)(s,X_s)ds+integral_0^t sigma_s f_x(s,X_s)dB_s, with all terms defined after the standard localizations.
items.strategy: First prove the formula for C^3 functions after stopping X, integral |b|, and integral sigma^2 inside deterministic compact bounds. Apply third-order Taylor on deterministic partitions; the first-order terms converge to the Lebesgue and Ito integrals, the quadratic term uses the already proved covariation theorem, and mixed, time-square, and cubic remainders vanish locally uniformly in probability by continuity, Cauchy-Schwarz, and maximal-mesh control. For f in C^{1,2}, choose a compact space-time cylinder strictly containing the stopped path range, multiply by a cutoff, extend across t=0 by the explicit C1 reflection 2f(0,x)-f(-t,x), and convolve with an explicit smooth product mollifier. On the smaller cylinder f_n, partial_t f_n, partial_x f_n, and partial_xx f_n converge uniformly to the corresponding derivatives. Apply the C^3 case and pass the drift terms by dominated convergence and the stochastic terms by Ito isometry plus the maximal bound. Then remove the localization. This is the binding C^3-first, localization-and-mollification route.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Theorem 5.79
Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.3

items.title: Multidimensional Ito formula for Brownian-driven processes
items.statement: Assume AC. Let X be an R^d-valued continuous Brownian Ito process dX=b dt+sigma dB driven by m-dimensional Brownian motion and let f belong to C^{1,2}([0,infinity) times R^d). Then, up to indistinguishability, for every t, df(t,X_t)=(f_t+sum_i b^if_i+(1/2)sum_{i,j}(sigma sigma^T)_{ij}f_{ij})dt+sum_{i,k} f_i sigma^{ik}dB^k, in the corresponding integral identity after localization.
items.strategy: First repeat the localized deterministic-partition argument for C^3 functions. Multivariable third-order Taylor supplies the remainder; first-order terms converge componentwise, and the already proved covariation theorem plus polarization identifies every Delta X^i Delta X^j term without falsely assuming independent diffusion coordinates. For C^{1,2}, cut off on a compact cylinder and use product mollifiers so f and exactly its time-first and space-first/second derivatives converge uniformly there. Dominated convergence handles drift, Ito isometry and the maximal bound handle stochastic terms, and localization is then removed.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Theorem 5.79

items.title: The Brownian square martingale
items.statement: Assume AC. B_t^2-t=2 integral_0^t B_sdB_s, hence B_t^2-t is a continuous martingale.
items.strategy: Use f(x)=x^2, b=0, sigma=1. Since E integral_0^T B_s^2ds=T^2/2, the integral is a genuine square-integrable martingale.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, equation (3.8)

items.title: The exponential Brownian martingale
items.statement: Assume AC. For theta real, Z_t=exp(theta B_t-theta^2t/2)=1+theta integral_0^t Z_sdB_s is a positive continuous martingale with E Z_t=1.
items.strategy: Ito cancels the drift. Factor Z_t/Z_s through the independent normal increment; its exponential moment is one, proving the true conditional martingale identity.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.3

items.title: Space-time harmonic functions yield Brownian local martingales
items.statement: Assume AC. If f in C^{1,2} satisfies f_t+(1/2)Delta f=0 on an open space-time domain, then f(t,B_t), stopped before leaving compact subdomains, is a continuous local martingale; square-integrable stopped gradients make it a true square-integrable martingale.
items.strategy: Ito cancels the drift and leaves integral grad f dB. Compact stopping bounds the gradient and gives a true martingale; exhaust the domain for the local statement.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Sections 3.3 and 3.6

items.title: Heat-semigroup martingales
items.statement: Assume AC. For bounded Borel g and fixed T, P_{T-t}g(B_t), extended at T by g(B_T), is a bounded martingale. For t<T, u(t,x)=P_{T-t}g(x) is smooth and solves u_t+(1/2)Delta u=0.
items.strategy: Markov gives M_t=E[g(B_T)|F_t], so tower proves the martingale. Differentiate the positive-time Gaussian convolution under the integral using Gaussian derivative bounds and the heat-kernel equation.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Sections 3.3 and 3.6

items.title: Characteristic exponential for a continuous local martingale with deterministic clock
items.statement: Assume AC. If M is a real continuous local martingale with M_0=0 and quadratic variation [M]_t=t, then for every real theta the bounded-on-finite-horizons process exp(i theta M_t+theta^2t/2), interpreted by real and imaginary parts, is a complex martingale.
items.strategy: Stop first at tau_n=inf{t:|M_t|>=n} wedge n. Deterministic-partition second-order Taylor applied to the real and imaginary parts gives the stopped complex local-martingale identity with compensator [M^{tau_n}]_t=t wedge tau_n: continuity and tightness of quadratic-variation sums kill the remainders, summation by parts identifies the weighted quadratic term, and stopped martingale-increment orthogonality plus uniform L2 bounds and the stated probability-to-L1 result justify conditional expectations. The stopped identities agree on overlaps and hence patch to exp(i theta M_t+theta^2t/2). Its modulus is the deterministic exp(theta^2t/2), bounded on each finite horizon, so the patched local martingale is a true complex martingale there. No incorrect t compensator is assigned after stopping.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Theorem 6.4

items.title: Levy characterization of Brownian motion
items.statement: Assume AC. A real continuous local martingale M with M_0=0 and [M]_t=t on a usual filtered space is Brownian motion with respect to that filtration.
items.strategy: Use the preceding characteristic-exponential martingale and divide its conditional identity at t by its F_s-measurable value to get the conditional characteristic function of M_t-M_s. Uniqueness gives N(0,t-s) independent of F_s; iterate for independent increments, then use continuity.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Theorem 6.4

items.title: Vector Levy characterization
items.statement: Assume AC. If continuous local M=(M^1,...,M^d) starts at zero and [M^i,M^j]_t=delta_ij t, then M is standard d-dimensional Brownian motion.
items.strategy: Every a dot M has quadratic variation |a|^2t and is scalar Brownian after normalization. Cramer-Wold and the conditional characteristic identities give joint normal increments independent of the past.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Corollary 6.5

items.title: The Brownian differential generator
items.statement: Assume AC. For f in C^2(R^d), write Lf=(1/2)Delta f for the Brownian Ito differential operator. This does not assert that every C^2 function lies in the closed-operator domain of the Brownian semigroup generator on C_0(R^d).
items.strategy: Read the dt coefficient from Ito's formula and explicitly separate this differential notation from semigroup-domain claims, which are outside scope.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.6

items.title: Dynkin formula for bounded Brownian stopping
items.statement: Assume AC. Let B be standard d-dimensional Brownian motion started at x, let tau be a bounded stopping time, and let f belong to C_c^2(R^d). Then E_x[f(B_tau)]=f(x)+E_x integral_0^tau Lf(B_s)ds.
items.strategy: Apply multidimensional Ito through t wedge tau. Compact support makes the gradient and Hessian bounded; bounded tau makes the stopped stochastic integral square-integrable with mean zero and the drift integrable. Take expectations and choose t beyond the deterministic bound for tau. No general local-martingale optional-stopping theorem or semigroup-domain claim is used.

items.title: Ito versus Stratonovich boundary
items.statement: Assume AC. This block uses left-endpoint Ito integration. Symmetric Stratonovich sums and their conversion rule are not defined here and belong to later stochastic calculus.
items.strategy: State the convention boundary and point to quadratic variation as the reason the ordinary chain rule cannot replace Ito's rule.

items.statement: Assume AC. Only continuous Brownian-driven processes are covered. Jump corrections, general semimartingales, SDE existence, Girsanov theory and stochastic geometry are outside this pair.
items.strategy: Record the precise scope boundary so Brownian formulas are not misread as general definitions or theorems.

items.title: A closed L2 subspace with trivial orthogonal complement fills L2
items.statement: Assume AC. If V is a closed linear subspace of real or complex L2(mu) and V perpendicular={0}, then V=L2(mu).
items.strategy: Choose a distance-minimizing sequence. Parallelogram makes it Cauchy; completeness and closedness give a minimizer v. Minimality under real and, in the complex case, imaginary scalar perturbations gives x-v perpendicular to V, hence x=v.

items.title: Brownian-filtration martingale representation
items.statement: Assume AC. In the usual augmented natural filtration of one-dimensional Brownian motion, every cadlag local martingale M equals M_0+integral H dB up to indistinguishability for a unique predictable locally square-integrable H modulo dt tensor P on localized horizons.
items.strategy: Fix T and let R_T be the range of terminal Ito integrals in mean-zero L2(F_T). Isometry makes R_T closed. For a mean-zero Z orthogonal to R_T, apply one-dimensional Ito separately to exp(q(t)/2)cos x and exp(q(t)/2)sin x along X_t=integral_0^t h_s dB_s for deterministic step h and q(t)=integral_0^t h_s^2ds. This proves the complex characteristic exponential is 1 plus an Ito integral, so orthogonality makes every finite Brownian-cylinder Fourier transform of the finite signed measure Z dP vanish. Fourier uniqueness, followed by a cylinder pi-system/Dynkin-lambda argument on the raw natural F_T and then the null-set completion step, gives Z=0. The closed-subspace lemma yields R_T=mean-zero L2(F_T). For an integrable Brownian-filtration martingale, truncate its terminal variable in L1; the L1 Doob inequality makes the bounded L2 represented martingales converge uniformly in probability, and a summable subsequence gives a continuous version. Apply this to each stopped piece of a cadlag local martingale, obtain compatible continuous versions, then stop those at continuous level exits to get L2 terminal variables. Represent the stopped pieces, use isometry to prove equality of their integrands on overlaps, and patch the predictable integrands along stopping intervals. Localization and the stopping identity yield the stated representation and uniqueness, without enlarging the usual Brownian filtration.

items.title: Square-integrable Brownian terminal variables have Ito representations
items.statement: Assume AC. For X in L2(F_T) in the usual Brownian filtration, X=E[X]+integral_0^T H_sdB_s for a unique predictable H in L2(dt tensor P).
items.strategy: Invoke directly the fixed-horizon closed-range surjectivity R_T=mean-zero L2(F_T) established as the first stage of the preceding representation proof, applied to X-E[X]. Terminal Ito isometry gives uniqueness. This avoids assuming a cadlag or continuous regularization for the process E[X|F_t] before representation supplies one.

items.title: Brownian-filtration local martingales have continuous versions
items.statement: Assume AC. Every cadlag local martingale in the usual augmented natural Brownian filtration has a continuous version, unique up to indistinguishability.
items.strategy: Representation identifies it with a continuous localized Ito integral. Continuous versions agreeing at each time agree on rationals on one full-probability event, hence everywhere.

items.title: Ito formula for Brownian powers
items.statement: Assume AC. For integer n>=2, B_t^n=n integral_0^t B_s^{n-1}dB_s+(n(n-1)/2)integral_0^t B_s^{n-2}ds; drift cancellation gives polynomial martingales such as B_t^2-t and B_t^3-3tB_t.
items.strategy: Apply Ito to x^n after stopping at |B|=m, then remove the stop using finite Gaussian moments. Apply space-time Ito to x^3-3tx for the cubic example.

items.title: Logarithm of geometric Brownian motion
items.statement: Assume AC. For x>0 and explicitly defined X_t=x exp((mu-sigma^2/2)t+sigma B_t), dX_t=mu X_tdt+sigma X_tdB_t and d log X_t=(mu-sigma^2/2)dt+sigma dB_t.
items.strategy: Apply Ito to the displayed exponential, then to log under compact positive localization. Positivity removes the localization; no SDE existence theorem is asserted.

items.title: Exponential martingale Brownian tail bound
items.statement: Assume AC. For a,T>0, P(sup_{t<=T}B_t>=a)<=exp(-a^2/(2T)).
items.strategy: Let tau_a be the first hit of a and take theta>0. Sample the positive exponential martingale on dyadic ceiling approximations to tau_a wedge T. Finite-grid optional sampling has expectation one, and Fatou gives E[Z_{tau_a wedge T}]<=1 without silently assuming continuous-time optional stopping. On the hitting event Z_{tau_a}>=exp(theta a-theta^2T/2), so Markov gives the bound; optimize at theta=a/T.

items.title: Harmonic functions of planar Brownian motion
items.statement: Assume AC. For planar Brownian motion, B_t^1B_t^2 and (B_t^1)^2-(B_t^2)^2 are continuous local martingales and become true martingales after bounded-domain stopping.
items.strategy: Compute Delta(xy)=Delta(x^2-y^2)=0 and apply the harmonic theorem. Bounded-domain stopping bounds gradients and makes the integrals square-integrable.

items.title: Expected exit time from an interval
items.statement: Assume AC. For a,b>0, Brownian motion started at x in (-a,b), and tau its first exit from (-a,b), E_x tau=(x+a)(b-x), hence E_0 tau=ab.
items.strategy: Let u(x)=(x+a)(b-x). Multiply u by the explicit C2 cutoff that is one on [-a,b], zero outside a slightly larger interval, and on each transition uses 1-10r^3+15r^4-6r^5; this gives a compactly supported C2 function agreeing with u near the stopped path. Apply bounded-stop Dynkin to tau wedge n, where Lu=-1 and u vanishes at the exit endpoints. Bounded convergence sends u(B_{tau wedge n}) to zero and monotone convergence yields the formula.

items.title: Hitting probabilities from an exponential martingale
items.statement: Assume AC. For a,b>0, x in (-a,b), and X_t=x+B_t+mu t, P_x(X exits (-a,b) at b)=(1-exp(-2mu(x+a)))/(1-exp(-2mu(a+b))) when mu is nonzero; for mu=0 it is (x+a)/(a+b).
items.strategy: For nonzero mu, exp(-2mu X_t) is a constant multiple of an exponential Brownian martingale. The LIL makes the drifted path tend in the sign of mu, so the continuous path exits in finite time. For C=(-infinity,-a] union [b,infinity) and tau=inf{t>=0:X_t in C}, continuity gives {tau<=t}=intersection_{m>=1} union_{q in Q intersection [0,t]}{dist(X_q,C)<1/m}: a hit implies the rational approximations, while on the compact interval [0,t] the reverse inclusion makes the continuous distance function attain its zero infimum. Since X is adapted, every event on the right lies in F_t, so the stopping-time definition applies directly without the Brownian-specific closed-hit lemma. Stop at tau wedge n; endpoint bounds give uniform integrability and dominated convergence, then solve the two-point expectation. For mu=0 invoke the earlier two-sided Brownian exit theorem directly (equivalently take the displayed continuous limit).

items.title: The ordinary chain rule fails for Brownian motion
items.statement: Assume AC. The rule d(B_t^2)=2B_tdB_t is false: B_t^2=2 integral_0^t B_sdB_s+t, and expectations distinguish the formulas for every t>0.
items.strategy: Use the square identity. The Ito integral has mean zero while E B_t^2=t, so omitting the quadratic-variation correction contradicts expectations.

items.title: An unbounded stopped exponential martingale needs uniform integrability
items.statement: Assume AC. Let Z_t=exp(B_t-t/2) and tau=inf{t:Z_t=1/2}. Then tau is finite almost surely and E Z_{t wedge tau}=1 for finite t, but Z_{t wedge tau} tends almost surely to 1/2. Thus the stopped family is not uniformly integrable and optional stopping at unbounded tau fails without UI.
items.strategy: The LIL gives B_t/t->0, hence log Z_t->-infinity; continuity makes tau finite. For fixed t, dyadic ceiling approximations to tau wedge t and the discrete optional-sampling identity give mean one. The sampled variables converge a.s.; Doob L2 applied to Z on [0,t], together with the finite Gaussian exponential moment of Z_t^2, makes sup_{s<=t}Z_s integrable, so dominated convergence yields E Z_{t wedge tau}=1. Yet Z_{t wedge tau}->1/2 a.s. Uniform integrability would promote this last convergence to L1 and preserve mean, a contradiction.
